sources.name: Financial Statements of the Government of New Zealand for the Year Ended 30 June 2025 (Treasury B.11), 'Fiscal Indicator Analysis - Expenses by Functional Classification'
sources.assumptions: All functional-classification categories below (health, education, etc.) and Finance costs are Core Crown actuals for FY2025 (excludes Crown entities/SOEs, e.g. Kaainga Ora, health entities - matches the scope this project's revenue side already taxes). Core Crown total expenses (excl. losses) is $141,675m, which these categories sum to exactly - Finance costs ($8,862m) is NOT one of the OECD functional categories but Treasury includes it in this same table so the total ties out; omitting it would silently under-count by ~$8.9bn, the same class of gap already found and fixed in this project's otherIndirectResidual. Figures converted from $NZDm to $K by x1000.

sources.name: Ministry of Social Development Annual Report 2025 (G.60), 'Benefits or Related Expenses' note, p.182
sources.assumptions: NZ Superannuation ($23,191,199k), Jobseeker Support and Emergency Benefit combined ($4,640,562k - MSD does not separate these), Sole Parent Support ($2,255,092k), Supported Living Payment ($2,668,450k), Accommodation Assistance ($2,232,026k), and a residual 'Other Benefits or Related Expenses' line ($1,057,867k, which bundles the Winter Energy Payment with other unspecified benefits - WEP's own figure can't be isolated from this table) are all real MSD actuals. These six lines sum to $36,045,196k, well short of the Treasury functional 'Social security and welfare' total below ($47,503,000k) - the gap is other MSD/Vote items never itemised here (e.g. disability allowance, student allowance) plus Working for Families (see next source), not a data error. Modelled as an explicit 'welfareResidual' component rather than silently dropped, mirroring this project's otherIndirectResidual precedent.

sources.date: 3 September 2025 (data extract, 2024 tax year = year ended 31 March 2024 - 2025 tax year not yet published)
sources.name: Inland Revenue - Working for Families statistics
sources.assumptions: Working for Families Tax Credits: $3,043m paid to 328,400 claiming families, 2024 tax year (year ended 31 March 2024). This is the same figure used in the FY2024 expenditure file, reused here only as an approximation since the 2025 IRD tax year hasn't been published yet - a genuine, flagged gap, not a real FY2025 actual. Per this project's convention (tax credits/exemptions belong under the tax they offset, not under expenditure), WFF is NOT one of the expenditure components below - it's subtracted out of the 'welfareResidual' component here so it isn't double-counted, and is intended to be modelled as a credit against income tax revenue instead.

sources.name: MSD Benefit Fact Sheets Snapshot, June 2025 Quarter
sources.assumptions: Recipient counts as at end of June 2025: Jobseeker Support 216,009; Sole Parent Support 79,953; Supported Living Payment 105,642. Used to back-derive each benefit's real $/year/recipient rate (spend / recipients) below, the same back-derivation technique already used elsewhere in this project (e.g. cgt/land/fbt base-from-revenue). NZ Superannuation recipient counts are not published in this text-extractable Snapshot table (MSD's NZS/Veteran's Pension client counts are Excel-only) - a genuine gap, not resolved here.

sources.name: Stats NZ - 'One million people aged 65+ by 2028'
sources.assumptions: 828,600 people aged 65+ (2023) is the only reasonably confirmed 65+ population figure found - used as a proxy for NZ Superannuation recipients (NZS is universal/non-means-tested for eligible residents 65+, so this is a reasonable stand-in, same technique as general.json's 15+ working-age proxy for UBI). Held flat across both FY2024 and FY2025 in this dataset since no separate per-year figure was obtainable via available tools - understates the true count given the growing 65+ cohort (Stats NZ projects 1 million by 2029), so the resulting $/year/recipient rate is itself an overestimate. A genuine precision gap, flagged rather than guessed at finer resolution.

sources.name: Stats NZ - National population estimates: At 30 June 2025
sources.assumptions: 5,324,700 - New Zealand's provisional estimated resident population at 30 June 2025, reported as 0.7% growth over the year. Used as the denominator for every 'direct spend' functional category's $/capita/year rate below - a genuine real unit, not an abstract %-of-baseline. Flagged precision caveat: this figure appears to be on a newer, post-2023-Census population base than the FY2024 file's 5,338,500 (2018-base) figure, and the two headline figures imply a small population *decrease* year-on-year that is more likely a base-methodology artifact than real - not independently resolved in this pass since Stats NZ's release pages could not be fetched in full (JS-rendered), only search-summarised.

sources.name: Stats NZ - Government finance statistics (general government): Year ended June 2025 (nominal expenditure GDP)
sources.assumptions: Nominal GDP $436,100m (year ended June 2025) used only for the informational 'defence as % of GDP' readout in meta, not for any expenditure calculation. Moderate confidence only - obtained via search-tool summarisation, not a direct fetch of the release tables. Also note: this FSGNZ-derived 'Defence' functional-expense figure ($3,271m, 0.75% of this GDP figure) is Core Crown *operating expenses* only - it is NOT the same thing as the internationally-reported ~1.19%-of-GDP 'defence spending' figure (SIPRI/World Bank series, most recently confirmed for 2024 only) that the real-world '2% of GDP' political target (2025 Defence Capability Plan) refers to, which likely includes capital/acquisition spending and a different Vote-level scope. Don't conflate the two - the %-of-GDP shown against this dataset's defence category will read much lower than the political target for that reason, not because of a data error.
